result.process_summary: Both the doorman and the firewall act as boundary controllers that enforce a set of explicit rules on entities attempting to cross the boundary. They inspect each entity, compare it against the rule set, and either allow passage or block it, thereby ensuring only authorized traffic (people or data) can enter or exit.
potential_breaks: A doorman is a single human agent, while firewalls can be distributed across multiple devices and operate at high speed.
The doorman deals with physical people and items, whereas a firewall deals with digital packets and protocols.
A doorman typically handles one person at a time, but firewalls process many simultaneous connections.
Outbound inspection may be less emphasized for a doorman than for a firewall, which often enforces both inbound and outbound policies.
